description: Using theories (technology acceptance model, TAM; stimulusorganism-response, SOR; elaboration likelihood model, ELM) in eWOM. Examining the relationship between eWOM, attitude, destination image, destination intention. Examining the motivations of active prosumers to engage in eWOM and share eWOM for hotels. Examining the relationship between tourist experience, image destination, satisfaction, and behaviour intention using qualitative methodology based on the eWOM of blogs. Analysing personality and need for self-enhancement that leads to eWOM intention.

Analysing tourist sentiments through eWOM data on platforms using qualitative methods. Analysing customers’ eWOM from Tripadvisor, using machine learning to analyse big data for hotels. Exploring tourists’ hotel satisfaction through eWOM from Tripadvisor using qualitative research methods. Examining how eWOM impacts customers’ travel behaviour.

Examining the relationship between eWOM, image brand, theory of planned behaviour (TPB), and customer behaviour. Analysing the elements that drive eWOM, and that establish eWOM credibility. Overall valence of a set of reviews (positive or negative). Examining single customer reviews and aggregate review scores; the perspective of both egos and whole networks.
Analysing the impact of eWOM in the destination and aWOM in the future. Examining the characteristics and factors of eWOM.
eWOM influencing trust in the destination and medical travel intention.
